title: The local supervisor could relaunch a killed durable runner
description:
A locally killed pi-durable runner settles its attempt failed: nudgeDue refuses every non-zero exit ('the runner failed'), so the attempt's durable storage — which runLocalWorker's harness.resume() is built to continue from — is abandoned on a kill, and the run pays a full redispatch with a fresh conversation. A bounded in-attempt relaunch of a durable runner after a signal death (the storage and the same requestId make it idempotent, 'the same argv replayed after a crash must find the same one again', harness/src/local/worker-host.ts) would give the local rung the mid-tool kill recovery the WorkerAgent host already has, and would make this tick's other delivery branch — a local harness kill that resumes in a new process without re-running the tool — provable in a real local run.
evidence: internal/exec/subprocess/nudge.go:216 (code != 0 -> "the runner failed"); internal/exec/subprocess/supervisor.go runTurn (a signal death settles runner.exit, no relaunch); harness/src/local/worker-host.ts:419 (harness.resume())
